title: Multi-country outbreak of mpox, External situation report #69 - 14 September 2026 - ReliefWeb

analysis.time: The report was published on 15 September 2026, with the event date being 14 September 2026. The outbreak data refers to July 2026 and the period from 6 July to 16 August 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak spans multiple countries across four WHO regions, with the highest number of cases reported in the WHO African Region. Specific countries mentioned include Madagascar, Angola, China, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Chile, Hungary, and others in Europe and the Americas.
analysis.event: A multi-country mpox outbreak was reported, with WHO conducting a global rapid risk assessment in August 2026. The outbreak is considered a graded emergency, with new outbreaks reported in multiple countries and over a thousand confirmed cases every month. Transmission is largely through sexual contact, often leading to household and community spread.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In July 2026, 32 countries reported 1370 confirmed mpox cases, including seven deaths (CFR 0.5%). About three-quarters of these cases were in the WHO African Region. Eleven African countries reported 1153 confirmed cases, including seven deaths (CFR 0.6%) in the last six weeks. The WHO assessed the global public health risk as moderate.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO continues to consider the outbreak a graded emergency and encourages sustained surveillance and coordinated preparedness. The Director-General’s recommendations on mpox have been extended until August 2027. A global initiative to improve vaccine access was launched in August 2026.

analysis.brief_en: This report from ReliefWeb, published on 15 September 2026, details a multi-country mpox outbreak assessed as moderate by the World Health Organization (WHO) in August 2026. The outbreak, considered a graded emergency, has seen over a thousand confirmed cases monthly, with the highest numbers in the WHO African Region. In July 2026, 32 countries reported 1370 cases, including seven deaths, with three-quarters of cases in Africa. Eleven African countries reported 1153 cases, including seven deaths, over the period from 6 July to 16 August 2026. Transmission is primarily through sexual contact, leading to household and community spread. The WHO has extended its recommendations on mpox until August 2027 and launched a global initiative to improve vaccine access in August 2026. The report emphasizes the need for sustained surveillance and coordinated response activities.

title: Health calls for public vigilance as mpox cases rise in SA

analysis.time: The Department of Health is urging citizens to remain vigilant of mpox symptoms as the country is experiencing a rapid increase in laboratory-confirmed mpox cases in the past few weeks. Of concern is that 13 of the total cases were recorded between 13 August and 17 September, which suggests a rapid local transmission of this preventable viral infection.
analysis.location_and_population: As of 17 September 2026, the country has recorded 18 confirmed and one probable case, and this requires immediate and sustained public cooperation to contain. The majority (15) of these cases were reported in the Western Cape, City of Cape Town in particular, 3 in Gauteng and 1 in KwaZulu-Natal.
analysis.event: One of the most recent cases involved an individual who travelled to Spain earlier this month and returned to South Africa on 14 September. This person underwent testing in Spain after being informed of his probable case status.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: All cases/patients range in age from 23 to 50 years, with a median age of 36.5 years, and 18 of them are males with only 1 female. Mpox is transmitted mainly through close physical contact with an infected person, including skin-to-skin contact with the rash or lesions, and contact with contaminated materials such as bedding, clothing, or towels used by an infected person.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: South African health authorities are in contact with the Spanish counterparts regarding laboratory test results of the individual to confirm his mpox status. The health authorities will decide where and how to use these doses to contain outbreaks. The government, through the support of the World Health Organization, has secured limited doses of mpox vaccines (MVA-BN) and treatment (Tecovirimat) as part of its outbreak response strategy to disrupt local transmission.

analysis.brief_en: The Department of Health in South Africa is calling for public vigilance as mpox cases have risen rapidly in the country. As of 17 September 2026, there have been 18 confirmed and one probable case, with the majority (15) reported in the Western Cape, particularly in the City of Cape Town, and 3 in Gauteng and 1 in KwaZulu-Natal. The surge in cases, with 13 recorded between 13 August and 17 September, indicates a quick local spread of the virus. All cases range in age from 23 to 50 years, with a median age of 36.5 and 18 males and 1 female. One recent case involved an individual who returned from Spain on 14 September and was tested there. South African health authorities are coordinating with Spanish counterparts to confirm the individual's status. The government has secured limited doses of mpox vaccines and treatment as part of its response strategy. Public cooperation, surveillance, and adherence to preventive measures are emphasized to curb further transmission. The virus spreads through close physical contact, including skin-to-skin contact with lesions and contaminated materials, and respiratory droplets during prolonged face-to-face contact. Individuals experiencing symptoms should seek medical attention immediately and avoid close contact with others.
